terms.meaning: A label such as Lab Report that tells the server how to process a file.
A medical imaging file format used for X-rays and scans.
Optical character recognition: software that reads text from an image.
A check that the uploaded file contains no malicious code.
A shared place in the app where data and actions such as uploads are kept.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the file and image pickers, navigation, layout pieces, icons, shared styles and parts, and the document store that does the actual upload.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup, with the upload work handled by the store.

sections.name: docTypes
sections.title: Document type options
sections.what: A fixed list of six document types (Lab Report, Prescription, Discharge, Imaging, Vaccination, Other), each with an icon and colour. The chosen type is sent with the file.
sections.why: Likely reason: the type tells the app how to process the file.
sections.watch_out: The type IDs are sent as they are, so they must match what the server accepts. This is not checked here.

sections.name: UploadScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Picking a file from the device
sections.what: Opens the file browser limited to PDF, images and DICOM, and keeps the chosen file's location, name and type. Also starts the camera flow, which asks for camera permission first and then names the photo with the current time.
sections.why: Likely reason: a file must be chosen before upload, and the camera asks permission first because the phone requires it.
sections.watch_out: Errors from the camera and gallery steps are not caught, unlike the file browser step, which is.

sections.name: UploadScreen: if
sections.title: Gallery pick and the upload action
sections.what: Lets the user pick a photo or video from the gallery and keeps it as the chosen file. The upload handler then sends the file to uploadDocument, shows a success message and returns home, or shows an error with the reason.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared handler lets any picked file be uploaded, and the server is expected to reject types it does not support.
sections.watch_out: The gallery allows videos even though the screen describes photos and documents, so the choice is wider than the screen says.

sections.name: UploadScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Upload area, progress bar and type picker
sections.what: Shows a dashed box that changes once a file is chosen, with buttons for Camera, Gallery and Files. While uploading it shows a percentage bar. Below it is a grid of the six document types with the chosen one highlighted.
sections.why: Likely reason: one tap area with three ways to add a file keeps the first step simple.
sections.watch_out: The progress bar takes only the first value in the progress list, so with more than one upload it could show another file's progress.

sections.name: UploadScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Processing note, upload button and styles
sections.what: Tells the user that a virus scan, text extraction and AI summary will follow the upload. Shows the Upload and Process button, which is disabled until a file is chosen and while uploading. Also holds the look settings for the screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets expectations about background processing, and the disabled button prevents an empty or repeated upload.
sections.watch_out: The button is disabled only by screen state, and there is no way to cancel an upload that is slow to finish.

summary: Lets the user pick a medical document from the camera, photo gallery or files, choose its type, and upload it to start processing.
purpose: Starts the path that takes a patient's paper or digital record into the app, where it is scanned and summarised.
why: Likely reason: three ways to add a file because people keep records in different places, and a document type so processing knows what the file is.
how: The user picks a file by camera, gallery or file browser, and the choice is kept on the screen. The user picks one of six document types, with Lab Report as the default. Pressing Upload and Process calls uploadDocument in the document store with the file location, name, file type and document type. On success it shows a message and returns to the home tab. On failure it shows the error text. A progress bar shows the upload percentage.
inputs: Photos from the camera, images from the gallery, PDF, image or DICOM files from the file browser, and the document type chosen by the user.
outputs: An upload started through the document store, a progress bar, a success or error alert, and navigation to the home tab.
risks: The camera and gallery actions do not catch errors, so a permission or picker failure may crash or do nothing. The 50 MB limit shown to the user is not checked in this file. The progress bar reads only the first upload in the progress list. The gallery accepts all media types, not only documents.
debug: If the upload fails, read the alert text, then check uploadDocument in documentStore and the server's upload endpoint. If the progress bar stays at zero or sticks, check the progress data the store provides. If the camera or gallery does nothing, check the permission prompt and the picker calls. If large files fail, check size limits on the server, since this file does not check them.
